svg.text: Federated Learning Engine (blue) · Unlearning Module (orange) · Privacy Certification Layer (green)
Authenticated submission · Rate-limiting · Tamper-evident audit log
Inputs: GDPR erasure requests, compromise alerts, client churn events
① Edge gradient updates → Fog → Cloud (training round)
② Global model broadcast → Fog → Edge (post-aggregation)
③ Targeted unlearn command (Cloud → specific Fog → SlideFU calibration on identified clients)
④ Adversarial channels (A₁ poisoning, A₂ BadUnlearn calibration, A₄ spurious deletion request flood)
Unlearning Module (SlideFU + UnlearnGuard) → DG₃ BadUnlearn resistance (ASR < 10%), DG₄ cost ≤ 30% retrain
Privacy Certification Layer → DG₂ Certified erasure (ε ≤ 1.0, MIA ≈ 50%)
Fog audit log + rate-limit → DG₅ Forensic auditability
A₁ Poisoning Client — gradients crafted during training (e.g., E₄)
A₂ BadUnlearn (Adversarial Unlearning Requester) — crafts updates during the unlearning round itself (e.g., E₁₀)
A₃ Honest-but-Curious Server — inspects aggregated gradients/calibration vectors at the cloud
A₄ Spurious Deletion Requester — floods authenticated deletion requests to exhaust the unlearning budget
(Defenses mapped to surfaces in Threat Model §3.3, integrated by FU-IDS components above)
